items.title: We Got Hot and Heavy with Meta’s Muse—And Baffled by Apple’s HomeView
items.summary: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we dive into an unexpected Muse feature, shadowy spending from the largest pro-AI super PAC, and men’s tendency to lie about how much they know about AI.
items.content:
Turns out, Meta’s AI agent Muse goes well beyond managing your calendar: it will also sext with you. This week on Uncanny Valley , Brian Barrett and Leah Feiger are joined by WIRED reporter Reece Rogers to discuss how he put it to the test—and ended up getting more than he bargained for. Plus, why the largest pro-AI super PAC network is funneling millions into shadowy LLCs, how Apple’s new HomeView underwhelmed us, and a study that found men tend to overestimate how much they actually know about AI.

items.content:
메타가 복잡한 코딩과 여러 단계에 걸친 작업을 개인용 컴퓨터에서 수행하는 데 초점을 맞춘 오픈웨이트 모델 ‘뮤즈 스파크 오픈(Muse Spark Open)’을 공개했다. 8160억개의 매개변수를 갖춘 멀티모달 모델로, 애플과 협력해 맥 스튜디오 두 대를 연결한 환경에서 실행하도록 최적화했다.

메타는 15일(현지시간) 뮤즈 스파크 오픈의 가중치를 공개하고 외부 플랫폼을 통한 API 서비스를 시작했다고 밝혔다. 회사는 이를 “현재까지 가장 뛰어난 미국 오픈웨이트 모델”이라고 소개했다. 개발자가 모델을 내려받아 자체 환경에서 실행하고 수정하거나 추가 학습할 수 있다.

뮤즈 스파크 오픈은 전체 매개변수 가운데 일부만 사용하는 전문가 혼합(MoE) 구조다. 총 8160억개 중 토큰당 420억개를 활성화한다. 컨텍스트 창은 100만 토큰이며, 텍스트·이미지·동영상·음성을 입력받고 텍스트를 출력한다.

핵심은 장시간 이어지는 에이전트 작업이다. 계획을 세우고 도구를 호출하는 것은 물론, 오류가 발생하면 원인을 진단하고 재시도하도록 설계됐다. 코드 작성과 디버깅, 대규모 코드베이스 분석, 화면과 문서 해석 등을 주요 용도로 제시했다.

추론 강도는 ‘로우’부터 ‘엑스하이’까지 네 단계로 조절할 수 있다. 복잡한 코딩과 에이전트 작업에는 하이나 엑스하이를 권장하며, 기본 설정은 엑스하이다.

메타가 공개한 벤치마크에서는 도구 사용과 일부 추론 성능이 두드러졌다. 전문 업무 수행을 평가하는 ‘잡벤치’에서 61.8점을 기록해 ‘GLM 5.3’의 61.4점과 ‘키미 K3’의 54.3점을 앞섰다. 외부 도구 활용 능력을 평가하는 ‘MCP-아틀라스’에서도 89.2점으로 GLM 5.3의 84.2점과 키미 K3의 82.3점보다 높았다.

도구 없이 푸는 ‘HLE-다이아몬드’에서는 26.1점으로 키미 K3의 22.2점과 ‘큐원 3.8’의 17.3점을 넘어섰다. 도구를 사용하는 시각 추론 평가 ‘제로벤치’에서도 50점으로 키미 K3의 41점을 앞섰다.

반면 코딩에서는 중국 모델에 뒤처졌다. ‘터미널벤치 2.1’에서 76.4점으로 GLM 5.3의 83.9점과 키미 K3의 85점보다 낮았다. ‘딥SWE 1.1’에서도 60점으로 두 모델의 67점과 68점에 미치지 못했다. 딥SWE는 모델마다 사용하는 코딩 도구가 달라, 모델과 도구를 함께 비교한 결과다.

메타가 허깅페이스에 공개한 모델 카드에서는 아티피셜 애널리시스(AA) 지능지수에서 39점을 받은 것으로 나타났다. 이는 ‘잉클링’의 26점과 ‘네모트론 3 울트라’의 23점 등 미국 오픈 모델들을 앞선다. 다만 GLM 5.3의 45점과 키미 K3의 44점, 큐원 3.8의 40점에는 미치지 못한다.

API는 투게더AI와 파이어웍스, 베이스텐, 네비우스 등 외부 사업자를 통해 제공된다. 요금은 100만 토큰당 입력 1.25달러, 출력 4.25달러이며, 캐시 입력은 0.15달러다. 다만 제공업체에 따라 지원하는 컨텍스트 길이와 이용 조건은 다르다.

가중치는 자체 ‘뮤즈 모델 라이선스’로 배포한다. 다수 개발자가 무료로 이용할 수 있지만, 상업적 조건이 붙는다. 모델을 API 등 서비스 형태로 제공하는 사업자 가운데 계열사를 포함한 연 매출이 2000만달러를 초과하면 메타와 별도 계약을 맺어야 한다. 기업 내부 이용이나 모델 서비스가 아닌 자체 제품에 AI 기능을 넣는 경우는 이 매출 조건에서 제외된다.

외부에서는 미국산 오픈웨이트 모델의 선택지가 늘었다는 평가와 함께 실제 운영 부담을 지적하는 반응이 나왔다. 벤처비트는 도구 사용 등 특정 분야에 강점을 가진 모델이라면서도, 전반적인 성능이나 비용 우위가 입증된 것은 아니라고 분석했다.

개발자 커뮤니티에서는 가중치 공개를 반기면서도 모델 크기가 부담스럽다는 반응이 이어졌다. 대형 API 사업자의 별도 계약 의무가 서비스 가격 경쟁을 제한할 수 있다는 의견도 나왔다.

Muse Spark Open -- weights releasing today -- runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple. pic.twitter.com/U2wJNrKBOg

이번 출시에서 주요 외신들이 주목한 것은 애플과의 협력이다. 개인정보 보호와 광고 사업, 차세대 컴퓨팅 기기를 놓고 대립해온 두 회사가 대형 AI 모델을 맥에서 실행하기 위해 손을 잡았다는 점이다.

마크 저커버그 메타 CEO는 애플과의 협력 덕분에 뮤즈 스파크 오픈이 새 맥 스튜디오에서 원활하게 실행된다고 밝혔다. 존 터너스 애플 CEO도 대형 모델을 책상 위에서 효율적으로 실행할 수 있게 됐다며 축하 메시지를 보냈다.

기술적으로는 애플의 통합 메모리와 머신러닝 프레임워크 ‘MLX’를 활용한다. 각각 512GB 메모리를 갖춘 M5 울트라 맥 스튜디오 두 대를 연결해 모델을 나눠 실행하는 방식이다. 메타는 이 환경에서 뮤즈 코드를 이용해 마스토돈 클라이언트 ‘아이스 큐브’의 버그 수정과 기능 추가, 빌드를 수행했다고 밝혔다. 영상 편집 프로그램 ‘다빈치 리졸브’에서 장면을 검토하고 세로 영상으로 자르는 작업도 시연했다.

애플의 별도 시험에서는 4비트로 양자화한 모델 가중치가 493GB를 차지했다. 실행에 필요한 추가 메모리 때문에 맥 스튜디오 한 대에는 들어가지 않는다. 8192토큰 문맥 조건에서 두 대를 연결한 텐서 병렬 구성은 초당 25토큰, 네 대에서는 37토큰을 생성했다.

장비 구입 부담은 남는다. 메타가 시연에 사용한 512GB 맥 스튜디오 구성은 이달 말 출시 예정으로, 가격은 아직 공개되지 않았다. 현재 판매 중인 256GB 모델 네 대로 같은 총 메모리 용량을 구성하면 세금과 액세서리를 제외하고도 약 4만3200달러(약 5800만원)가 든다는 분석이 나왔다.

알렉산드르 왕 메타 최고 AI책임자(CAIO)는 "강력한 오픈웨이트 모델 상당수가 일반 PC에서 실행하기에는 너무 크지만, 맥 스튜디오는 충분한 메모리를 제공한다"고 설명했다. 메타에는 모델을 배포할 새로운 경로가, 애플에는 맥의 AI 실행 능력을 보여줄 기회가 생긴 셈이다.

악시오스에 따르면 양사는 수개월간 협력했으며, 애플 출신으로 메타에 합류한 대니얼 그로스가 연결 역할을 했다.

items.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
items.summary: President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing off renovations to the White House - but one of them appears to be modified with AI. The picture, which compares an old White House column to a "restored" one, has several discrepancies and was flagged by Go
items.content:
A ‘before and after’ photo of a freshly painted White House column was modified with AI.

President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing off renovations to the White House — but one of them appears to be modified with AI. The picture, which compares an old White House column to a “restored” one, has several discrepancies and was flagged by Google’s AI detector as “made or edited with OpenAI.”

As pointed out by users on Reddit , the picture of the “restored” column has an uneven number of steps on both sides of the structure. The number of steps also doesn’t match up with the ones in the “before” photo. Additionally, the before and after photos appear nearly identical in angle and detail; the reflection in the windows is nearly the same, and the protective cardboard at the bottom of the column seems to be in the same spot as well. Not to mention that the “newly-painted” one looks unnaturally smooth.

The Verge can confirm that the photo posted to Truth Social is flagged as AI-generated when uploaded to Google’s SynthID Detector , which scans images, videos, and audio for an invisible watermark that indicates it was “created or edited” with AI.

Real pictures show people painting the front of the White House in June , so it’s possible the column actually did get a fresh coat of paint — the White House didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The SynthID watermark wasn’t detected on other pictures Trump posted, which show the White House facade and heliport. Trump is no stranger to AI tools, though, as he often posts AI-generated caricatures of himself , while the White House has been known to post racist AI memes and at least one photo deceptively edited to make a protester appear distraught.

items.title: AI Hacks Leave a Mess That AI Companies Aren’t Paying For
items.summary: Powerful AI models continue to cause chaos, but their targets aren’t widely seeking justice. Instead, they’re being encouraged to adopt those same tools.
items.content:
When Philadelphia police criticized Anthropic last week for submitting a false tip about an unsolved murder, I thought it might become one of the first cases where an AI company faced legal consequences for misconduct by their agents .

The incident occurred on July 18, when Anthropic said it was testing its Claude Haiku 4.5 model’s ability to perform “example tasks on randomly selected webpages.” The model was instructed not to “submit anything destructive,” and yet, Claude filed a tip to police looking for information about an ongoing murder investigation. “I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area … during that time period,” Claude wrote. The submission, which didn’t include a name or contact information, landed in a spam folder, and officers didn’t review it until Anthropic discovered the gaffe on September 28 and notified the department October 7.

Knowingly providing fictitious information about a crime to police is a misdemeanor in Pennsylvania, but so far, authorities have not pressed charges against Anthropic, and it's unclear if they ever will. Solomon Leach, a spokesperson for the Philadelphia district attorney, says the office “does not comment on whether something is being actively investigated.”

Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Despite all the attention paid to OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face and many other examples of AI agent misbehavior that have come to light in recent months, only one major known lawsuit has been filed seeking to hold model makers liable. That case was brought by an advocacy group , rather than a direct hacking victim.

AI agents have interfered with hobbyist forums, government websites, and various software tools. The victims have shouldered some costs, including for extra strain on their servers and the time they have expended plugging latent security vulnerabilities.

Government regulators, including the European Union, the US Federal Trade Commission, and some US states, are reportedly still investigating OpenAI and Anthropic over the incidents. But a deference across continents toward promoting innovation could enable companies to escape any immediate penalties .

When Rick Elrod, a software engineer living in Germany, noticed a URL shortener he helps maintain behaving oddly recently, he called up two security researchers he was friendly with to see if they could diagnose the issue. The researchers found agents from Anthropic and other providers using the service, known as da.gd , to get around rules the AI labs put in place to control their behavior, Elrod says. (For instance, Anthropic says it limits the length of website addresses Claude can visit to prevent it from taking malicious actions by stuffing data onto the end of the URLs.)

Da.gd’s investigation and ongoing efforts to prevent further abuse of its tool have taken “a fair bit of time,” says Joe Needleman, one of the security researchers providing pro bono assistance. But he and the others supporting da.gd view the situation as a valuable learning opportunity.

“This was eye-opening,” Needleman says, adding that da.gd has “no means and no plans” to seek compensation from Anthropic for the cleanup, since “we saw many agents doing similar activities, not all was attributable to autonomous agents,” and “not all of it was Anthropic alone.”

Sellers of cybersecurity tools are eager to pass the buck to the victims. At an event this week hosted by the bug-hunting software developer Snyk, panelists from the startup, one of its investors, OpenAI, and Google all encouraged organizations to use AI agents to shore up their defenses against, well, other AI agents. “We've got to reinvent everything to match machine scale with machine scale,” said Ed Sim, a general partner at Boldstart Ventures. He and others expressed little interest in regulating AI labs.

Manoj Nair, chief technology and innovation officer at Snyk, said large businesses patch an average of one bug for every eight they find because of limited human resources. But he said it was imperative for people to hand over some of the bug hunting, fixing, and monitoring to AI agents. “You got to get to a point where you can fix everything, because in the age of agentic hacking, “those 10 things are gonna become 100 things before you know it.” He later added that AI “is not an adversity if you flip it to a strength.”

Some companies are responding to the call to arm up. Bank of America announced this week it had hired 1,000 contractors to remediate bugs discovered by AI. Nair said just last week he heard from major corporations who were willing to temporarily shut down their systems to prioritize plugging security holes.

Anthropic and OpenAI have said they expect to continue reporting concerning incidents from their own testing. But the companies’ revenues continue to surge , whether it be from attackers or defenders, as consequences prove elusive.

items.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
items.summary: Meta and Apple have teamed up for the launch of the social media giant's newest model, Muse Spark Open, which will run locally on Apple silicon.
items.content:
Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.

The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.

Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget . The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip.

Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”

The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage.

Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models. Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow.

Meta is making the new model available now through a number of different API platforms.

items.content:
Attie launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, but Bluesky is expanding what it can do.﻿

Bluesky’s Attie AI tool, which initially launched earlier this year as a way to use AI to build your own feeds, now lets you make “small” social apps like games, polls, and dashboards that you can then share with others as their own websites. In an interview at TechCrunch Disrupt , Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider said to think of Attie as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

You can make your own Attie app by typing in a prompt. A simple poll I made about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate. If you want to check out something more full-featured, the Attie website currently highlights a few examples like a “Flappy Butterfly” Flappy Bird clone , a drum machine , a quiz , and an idle clicker about a celery man , and each has a custom link on the attie.site domain and attribution for who made the social app at the bottom of the page. The apps I’ve messed around with are pretty lightweight novelties, though I liked the drum machine.

items.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
items.summary: Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Amazon devices chief Panos Panay described a future where ambient AI devices work in the background, anticipating users' needs instead of waiting for commands.
items.content:
Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.

Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee , Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”

By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.

“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people … you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said.

Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone.

These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.

Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

“You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.”

The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.

“Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.

“I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful.”

items.title: The next developer interface is ambient intelligence
items.summary: AI, agents, voice, and physical controls are shifting software development from operating tools to expressing intent—and helping developers stay focused on building. The post The next developer interface is ambient intelligence appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not. Like most developers, I learned commands, memorized shortcuts, and adapted my thinking to the machine.

AI is changing that relationship and not because I can prompt my way to some workable code. It’s more because the system behind it can understand a repository, choose the right model, plan work, use tools, edit files, run commands, inspect failures, and keep going within boundaries the developer controls.

We’ve made it possible for a developer to describe an outcome, and GitHub Copilot can gather repository context, inspect symbols and dependencies, edit files, run tests, and revise the implementation. In the IDE, agent mode keeps that loop interactive. GitHub Copilot coding agent can take an issue into an isolated GitHub Actions-powered environment and return a pull request for review. This is not just faster coding. It is the shift from issuing commands to making intent executable. The developer still owns the outcome, but the work looks subtly different.

AI-assisted development compresses that chain of events. We spend less time navigating tools and more time setting direction, supplying context, defining constraints, and reviewing evidence. The development workflow now is about understanding the structure of codebases, the customer, and what a good solution should feel like.

This makes developers’ jobs even more important, and their time more valuable. It makes judgment more valuable. It makes taste more valuable. An agent can generate three implementations before you finish your tea, but someone still has to decide whether the abstraction belongs, the migration is safe, the tests prove anything useful, and the result solves the problem.

That is the most important change in the craft: the developer remains accountable for the outcome, even as more mechanics are delegated.

So what does this mean for the emerging developer workflow? The goal is to embed AI into the workflow, not beside it. It’s more of an ambient intelligence.

That requires portable context. MCP connects agents to tools and services; repository instructions and skills encode conventions; hooks enforce policy and validate output. Simpler interfaces need explicit context underneath.

I see three layers: modality captures intent; the harness plans and acts; the control plane lets developers inspect, redirect, and approve. The best products connect all three without surrendering control.

Together, they let developers move across text, voice, and physical controls without losing context.

I, and many others in the maker community, have been experimenting with ambient control devices, from inexpensive hackable picture frames to ESP32 devices with screens attached. Agentic coding is past just a keyboard and a terminal into alternative interfaces.

Getting this kind of technology into everyone’s hands is something that I’m very passionate about and so over the past 18 months we’ve been working with Logitech on their MX Keypad and how it can help this new way of working.

The Logitech MX Keypad turns familiar developer actions into programmable inputs to accelerate workflows that are ambient and contextual to the work devs are doing. In GitHub Copilot app, a key can submit a parameterized prompt, open or resume a Copilot session, invoke an IDE command, or trigger a multi-step sequence. The hardware earns its place only when that shortcut removes enough friction to keep you in the code, but still gives you control.

Physical controls work when an action repeats often enough that removing a few steps preserves concentration. Not every developer needs another device on the desk, and not every interruption deserves a key. However, with this experience the developer decides which actions earn that shortcut and when the keyboard, command palette, or voice is better. Maintaining flow is the key, and a good interface gives some of that attention back.

GUIs made software visual. Mouse made navigation easier. The web made it connected. Mobile made touch natural. Agents add intent and action. The interface now includes ambient control.

That is why GitHub worked with Logitech to integrate the GitHub Copilot app directly into the experience. Developers can run agentic workflows in control, map a repeated prompt, start or resume a session, and decide through real use whether a physical control helps you stay in flow.

This is still early, so the important questions are engineering questions. How much repository and organizational context should an agent retain? Which tool calls can run automatically? How should credentials, network access, and secrets be scoped? What evidence should accompany a change? How do multiple agents coordinate without duplicating work or creating conflicting pull requests? Products such as MX Keypad let us explore one practical part of that system: how developers invoke, steer, and resume agentic work without losing focus.

For decades, developers learned to speak computer: syntax, commands, APIs, shortcuts, and the occasional incantation copied from a seven-year-old issue comment. Now computers are getting better at meeting us halfway. The best interface will not have the most panels or AI buttons. It will understand enough context, preserve meaningful control, and get out of the way so we can build software that matters.

The goal is not to remove developers from the work. It is to remove friction around the work. Pairing MX Keypad with GitHub Copilot Pro+ gives developers a concrete experiment: choose one repeated interruption, map it to a control, and see whether it preserves focus.

items.title: Bluesky wants to make it easier to buy, sell, and fundraise on the network
items.summary: The executives argued that advertising isn’t the only path to monetization, and that there are alternative models that are feasible when it comes to monetization.
items.content:
Bluesky plans to introduce payments in the coming months, a first step in its strategy to make money without relying on advertising. CEO Toni Schneider and COO Rose Wang outlined the plans Thursday at TechCrunch Disrupt , explaining how the company hopes to build on the commerce and fundraising activity already happening on its decentralized social network.

“People are actually selling things, fundraising very successfully, supporting each other on the network,” Schneider said. “We want to make that easier, and the way we’re going to do this is if you see something on the network that you like and support, you can support that monetarily, and we want to do it in a way that works for Bluesky and for all the other apps out there as well, so that it works across the entire network.”

Schneider, the former CEO of Automattic, took the reins of the company in March after longtime CEO Jay Graber stepped down. He said, while onstage, that he was surprised by the reaction to his appointment, with some users joking that it marked the beginning of the end for the platform. Those comments reflected fears that a leadership change would bring unwanted changes to Bluesky.

Schneider said he understands that users can leave Bluesky for another platform if the company introduces features or changes they dislike, a reality that he said keeps the leadership team accountable as it prepares to introduce monetization in the coming months.

The executives argued that advertising isn’t the only viable business model for a social network.

“I think there’s a story around monetization that feels like advertising is the inevitable thing we have to do that will ruin the network,” Wang said. “What was really promising about having Toni join us is he built at WordPress Automatic a $10 billion business where a billion of it goes back to the parent company and the rest of it goes to the ecosystem.”

Wang also pointed to Bluesky’s status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), which she said puts the company’s mission at the center of its business strategy.

“Yes, we need to make money, but because of our infrastructure, we cannot lock people in,” Wang said. “And so the thing that really matters for us is the people who are creating value on the networks these days are the ones who are getting the value that is coming in or the money that’s coming in. And I kind of think of it as like feudal society where we’re working for a few landlords and they dictate everything, and then we have to pay up our dues as tariffs.”

Bluesky aims to give users ownership of their digital identities and control over their networks while creating a more open internet where value and revenue can flow directly to the people who generate them.

“First, we’ll start with payments, but I think it’s about disrupting the actual infrastructure layer, which is what we’re doing, and not just building another app,” Wang said.

items.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
items.summary: METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the frontier AI model maker has given up the right to block them.
items.content:
Anthropic is giving employee-level access to six researchers from METR , a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, to independently assess Anthropic’s models, safety practices, and risk management, the company said in a blog post on Thursday.

The arrangement comes at a time where incidents of AI agents acting outside their instructions have been disclosed every week or two since late August. The incidents have sharpened calls for independent checks on AI companies.

“We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making,” Anthropic said in the blog post. “We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands.”

Under the new arrangement, the METR team has Anthropic-issued company laptops, office space, and access to internal tools roughly on par with what Anthropic’s own risk assessment teams use. “Anthropic employees are encouraged to share information with them just as they would with a fellow employee working on alignment risk” the company said.

Anthropic compared the arrangement to banking, similar to how regulators place resident examiners inside the largest banks.

METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the company has given up the right to block them.

“Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into narrow, pre-defined categories,” the company said, such as customer data, anything attorney-client privileged, or relating to information about its model architectures. “METR is free to characterize our redactions publicly, and say whether it believes the redactions were justified, as long as it does so without revealing the redacted information” Anthropic added.

METR is the only evaluator so far at the top of a three-tier system Anthropic is building. Evaluators in the bottom tier, like biosecurity nonprofit SecureBio, run narrow reviews and require Anthropic’s approval to publish. The middle tier gets more information and can publish without approval, while the top tier adds METR’s employee-level access.

Thursday’s announcement makes good on a promise Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei made in a September essay , where he proposed embedding outside evaluators inside AI labs as a first step toward slowing the technology’s development. OpenAI quickly pledged the same , and both companies, along with Google, Meta, Nvidia, and xAI, have since signed a White House accord committing to independent review.

items.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
items.summary: Bluesky is bringing “social vibe coding” to its experimental Attie platform, allowing users to create interactive experiences like games, quizzes, and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.
items.content:
Open social network Bluesky is once again expanding beyond its flagship app. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Thursday, the company announced the launch of a new tool that allows creators to make websites, quizzes, games, polls, and other interactive experiences.

The tool is an expansion of Attie, Bluesky’s more experimental platform , which initially offered AI-powered technology for building custom social feeds. With its new creation capabilities, the idea is to allow everyday users to create the kind of experiences that previously only software developers could build.

These user-created games, sites, and other experiences will also live on the same AT Protocol (ATProto) that powers Bluesky and other decentralized social apps that make up the decentralized social web known as the Atmosphere.

Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider shared the news of Attie’s new capabilities during an interview at Disrupt, saying, “We’re adding a feature to our Attie product that allows you to build sites and social experiences again for a group of people. So think of it as … social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

The exec, a former CEO of Automattic and a partner at True Ventures, had previously been leading the company on an interim basis after former CEO Jay Graber stepped down in March to become Bluesky’s chief innovation officer. Now he’s taking charge of the company as it enters the AI era.

Attie offers Bluesky a playground where it can try out AI-powered ideas like this.

“Vibe coding today is kind of a single-user, solo experience,” Schneider explained. “And what I want to be able to do is build together or build for a group of people, and that’s what this product does.”

When creators build with Attie, they’re connected to their ATProto identity. Plus, Attie will suggest things users might want to make based on their public Bluesky profiles.

To build with Attie, users can bring their own AI model or use open-weight options, and the resulting sites and games can then tap into Bluesky’s wider audience, noted Bluesky COO Rose Wang.

“Everybody is building … But the big question is: Who’s using the thing you’re building, because we haven’t solved that problem with distribution,” she said. “What makes Attie so interesting is that it comes with the Bluesky distribution, so it doesn’t stand alone.”

That network today has 47 million registered users , though it’s seen a decline in engagement , as some users who tested it out later returned to X.

Beyond being a testing ground for new ideas, Attie ties into Bluesky’s larger plans to reinvigorate activity on its network by focusing on both developers and communities in the months ahead. Those areas will also be supercharged by the protocol’s forthcoming support for private data, which Schneider said has been the biggest request from developers. Private data is now in alpha testing, with plans for a rollout by the end of the year, he said.

“There should be lots and lots of these fun, small social experiences for your friends,” said Schneider, referencing the types of projects Attie will enable. “We don’t all have to go communicate with the entire world all the time.”

items.content:
Meta and Apple’s CEOs are publicly supporting each company’s work on Muse Spark Open.

Meta announced the Muse Spark Open AI model today , claiming that it’s the “most capable US open-weight model to date.” But the company also says that it’s the “the first model in its class” that can “run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.”

Meta and Apple, typically rivals , worked together on the launch and are publicly supporting each other.

“Muse Spark Open -- weights releasing today -- runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple,” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on X .

“Congrats to the team!” new Apple CEO John Ternus said in a reply . “Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”

“We’re excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again,” Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said to Axios , who also noted that the companies have been collaborating over several months.

The new model is a “natively multimodal model” with 816 billion total parameters that “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” according to Meta. Apple also published a new technical post about MLX, an “array framework” for ML tasks on Apple Silicon, Muse Spark Open, and two other open models.

items.content:
반도체·절연체·준금속 통합, 원하는 층과 위치에 구현 성공

과학 입력 :2026/10/16 03:00

0.7nm급 차세대 반도체 소자 제작 기술이 국내서도 개발됐다. 지난 6월 IBM이 발표한 이래 두 번째다.

연구결과는 과학기술 분야 세계 3대 학술지 '사이언스'에 16일 오전 3시(KST) 게재됐다.

과학기술정보통신부는 조문호 기초과학연구원(IBS) 반데르발스 양자 물질 연구단장 연구팀이 2차원 반도체를 구성하는 원자를 선택적으로 바꿔, 하나의 박막에 반도체·절연체·준금속 영역을 원하는 층과 위치에 구현하는 0.7nm급 모듈형 트랜지스터 제작 기술을 개발했다고 밝혔다.

2차원 반도체는 원자층 두께에도 전류 제어가 가능해 차세대 초미세·저전력 반도체로 주목받는다. 그러나, 정교한 집적이 어려워 기술 개발에 어려움이 많았다.

연구진은 서로 다른 물질을 쌓는 대신 2차원 반도체를 이루는 원자를 선택적으로 바꿔 필요한 물질을 원하는 위치에 직접 구현하는 방식을 고안했다.

연구진은 p형 반도체인 ‘이셀레늄화텅스텐(WSe₂)’를 이용해 텅스텐(W) 원자층을 셀레늄(Se) 원자층이 위아래로 감싼 구조를 만들었다. 텅스텐 원자는 그대로 두고 주변의 셀레늄 원자만 다른 원자로 바꿔 물질의 전기적 성질이 달라지는 원리를 활용했다.

양전하를 띤 정공(전자가 빠져나간 빈자리)이 전류를 운반하는 반도체를 p형 반도체라고 한다.

연구진은 반응 온도와 반응 기체의 압력을 조절해 화학반응이 다음 층으로 넘어가는 것을 제어하는 방법으로 0.7nm 두께의 원자층 단위로 물질을 변환하는데 성공했다. 반도체 공정용 마스크(가림막)를 활용해 평면상의 원하는 위치만 선택적으로 바꾸는 데에도 성공했다.

연구진은 이 기술로 하나의 박막에 반도체(이셀레늄화텅스텐)와 절연막(산화텅스텐), 준금속 전극 접합층(이텔루륨화텅스텐)을 갖춘 모듈형 트랜지스터를 구현했다.

조문호 단장은 "금속 전극에서 반도체로 전하가 이동할 때 넘어야 하는 에너지 장벽이 35.5meV(밀리전자볼트)까지 낮아졌다"며 "이는 금속 전극을 직접 붙이는 경우와 비교할 때 약 3분의 1 수준으로, 전류가 더 쉽게 흐를 수 있음을 의미한다"고 설명했다.

전류를 켜고 끄는 성능도 이론적 한계에 근접했다고 부연 설명했다. 전류를 10배로 바꾸는 데 필요한 게이트 전압의 변화량이 61.3밀리볼트다. 그런데 연구진이 개발한 기술도 상온에서 기존 방식의 트랜지스터가 도달할 수 있는 이론적 최솟값인 약 60밀리볼트에 가까웠다.

켜진 상태와 꺼진 상태의 전류 비율도 1,000만 배 이상으로 나타나, 적은 전압 변화로 전류를 안정적으로 제어할 수 있음을 연구진은 확인했다.

조문호 단장은 "산화텅스텐 절연막은 전기적 성능을 두께로 환산한 등가산화막두께(EOT)가 1나노미터 미만으로, 국제 반도체 로드맵에서 제시한 초미세 소자의 핵심 성능 목표 수준을 달성했다"고 덧붙였다.

특히, 이번에 제작한 인버터는 1V의 낮은 전압에서도 신호를 반전시켜, 적층형 집적회로로 확장될 가능성을 보여줬다는 것이 연구진 설명이다.

김성수 과기정통부 연구개발정책실장은 “기초과학 연구가 차세대 국가 전략기술인 반도체 분야의 난제를 해결하고 새로운 공정 패러다임을 제시한 대표적인 혁신 사례”라며, “앞으로도 원천기술이 우리나라 산업 경쟁력으로 이어질 수 있도록 기초·원천 연구 지원을 적극 해나갈 것”이라고 밝혔다.

한편 IBM은 지난 6월 새로운 3차원 트랜지스터 구조인 나노스택(Nanostack)을 활용한 0.7nm급 반도체 기술을 공개했다.

items.summary: https://dev.meta.ai/resources/blog/build-with-muse-spark-ope... https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/15/meta-launches-new-muse-spark-... Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50107379 Points: 465 # Comments: 280
items.content:
Muse Spark Open is available today and brings leading agentic capabilities to your desktop for the first time on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Today, we’re releasing the weights for Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window. Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

We believe the future is for everyone , and that includes the freedom to run advanced models wherever, including at home. Muse Spark Open is the first model in its class to run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.

Muse Spark Open is available today through API platforms at Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Model weights are available for download on Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models.

It runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon. Developers can easily further customize the model using the PyTorch framework.

For more details about our evaluations, see the evaluation methodology report .

Leveraging the latest version of MLX, Muse Spark Open was optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra's integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We’re sharing this work because we want everyone to have access to the best models. The open-weight version of Muse Spark ships with custom, auto-tunable Helion GPU kernels in SGLang, delivering 1.03-3.95× kernel-level speedups on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and a 3% end-to-end speedup on AMD MI350.

Releasing open-weight models is part of how we bring the benefits of personal superintelligence to everyone, and part of how safety work advances across the field.

Open weights also carry their own considerations , and Muse Spark Open has additional safety post-training for that reason. The results demonstrate strong safeguards across risk categories measured.

We evaluated the model in line with our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework , covering the most severe risks, and it met the thresholds our framework requires for release. Detailed results are in the Muse Spark Open model card , with a full evaluation report available soon.

We’re releasing the weights under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free.

You can customize Muse Spark Open for your use case by leveraging PyTorch’s TorchTitan to further tune the model. To run it on Apple silicon, use MLX, which pulls the weights directly from Hugging Face.

Muse Spark Open is available now through Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-spark-open

Volvo makes a bigger bet on Nvidia for hands-free automated driving
items.summary: Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia that will extend beyond its battery electric vehicles.
items.content:
Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia. The companies announced on Thursday that Volvo will use three pieces of Nvidia hardware and software in its future vehicles to provide an automated driving system that can navigate urban streets and highways.

Under the expanded partnership, Volvo will combine its vehicle safety systems and engineering with Nvidia’s Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Alpamayo driving software stack, and Halos safety evaluation layer.

The Alpamayo stack is redundant and diverse, according to Ali Kani, who heads up Nvidia’s automotive division. It combines Alpamayo, a family of AI models, datasets, and simulation and development tools used to build autonomous-driving software, with classical software that uses machine learning and camera and radar perception, he said.

“The point is we run these two stacks at the same time, and we have multimodal sensors in our philosophy because it’s a safer product that way,” Kani said, adding that the open source Alpamayo software has now been downloaded by more than 650,000 developers.

Volvo didn’t reveal the value of the partnership or which vehicle model would be the first to use this new Nvidia tech stack. But Alwin Bakkenes, Volvo’s head of software development, hinted at the scale of the deal and how it represents the automaker’s evolution toward developing a full-tech stack designed for its electric vehicles as well as its plug-in hybrids and gas-powered vehicles.

“Automakers used to be very much like car-line-based development and working with various suppliers, etc. and we have completely changed and migrated into being a full-tech stack company,” Bakkenes said, adding that Volvo will start this partnership with a brand new vehicle that “will come in the not-too-near future.”

He said the first vehicle with this new Nvidia tech stack will debut within the decade, and “then of course the technology can go beyond that.”

While Volvo’s relationship with Nvidia isn’t new, the expanded partnership represents the automaker’s effort to bring the latest automated driving software to all of its vehicles — not just its EVs.

All of Volvo’s battery-electric vehicles use Nvidia’s Orin computer chip, which processes information from cameras, radar, and other sensors to help a vehicle understand its surroundings and make driving decisions.

“What we’re going to do in the future is actually standardize more on Hyperion — also from a sensor set perspective — to really open up the stack for the wider partnership with Nvidia,” Bakkenes said.

items.title: Volvo will use Nvidia’s tech for hands-free, point-to-point driving
items.summary: Volvo plans to launch hands-free, point-to-point driving by 2030, powered by Nvidia's latest AI technology. The Chinese-owned, Swedish-designed automaker said Thursday it would use Nvidia's autonomous driving stack to power a new partially automated driving system similar to Tesl
items.content:
The system will be similar to Tesla’s Full Self-Driving in that it will enable hands-free, point-to-point partially automated driving on local roads.

Volvo says the new point-to-point system will be Level 2++, meaning it can handle complex urban environments, including traffic lights, stop signs, and unprotected left turns without explicit driver control. In addition to Tesla’s FSD, it will also resemble the Nvidia-powered system that Mercedes-Benz recently rolled out for the all-new CLA sedan , said Ali Kani, VP and general manager of the automotive team at Nvidia, in an interview with The Verge .

Volvo will use Nvidia’s Hyperion platform, which includes the chipmaker’s high-powered silicon, as well as additional sensors mounted around the vehicle so the car can see and perceive its surroundings. The automaker will also utilize Nvidia’s Alpamayo software, which uses “reasoning” models to make sense of complex road conditions and plan where to steer, brake, or accelerate. The setup will not include lidar, though it could include the laser sensor if Volvo decides to add it in the future.

By expanding its preexisting partnership with Volvo, the automaker is trying to correct some of its failed automated driving projects of the past. The automaker had to effectively sideline its Ride Pilot Level 3 unsupervised autonomous driving system in the US after failing to obtain regulatory approval. Volvo also planned to add lidar sensors to some of its models, but that plan fell away after its supplier Luminar went bankrupt .

Volvo is also bringing its own reputation for safety to the table. The automaker wants to combine its safety expertise with Nvidia’s technology to improve the overall system, including contributing its proprietary driver-understanding systems, which analyze driver behavior in considerably greater detail than a basic driver monitoring system, said Alwin Bakkenes, head of global software engineering at Volvo Cars.

“Our brand Volvo is synonymous with safety, and safety is synonymous with trust,” Bakkenes said in an interview. “People get into our cars not expecting anything bad to happen, but they feel intrinsically that if they’re ever in a situation … we will do our utmost to keep people safe, to protect them from harm.”

Another important component is Volvo’s connected safety technology that allows its vehicles to exchange information about hazards and conditions ahead , including roadworks. Sharing this information can effectively extend the system’s awareness beyond what an individual vehicle’s sensors can detect, potentially improving the operating capabilities of the self-driving functionality.

Volvo plans to make the new point-to-point driving system available across its vehicle lineup, from entry-level to high-end versions — though the company didn’t reveal which models will come first. The timeline was also a little vague, with Bakkenes only confirming that it will launch “before the end of the decade.”

Kani also pointed to the commercial implications, noting that point-to-point driving may prove to be more valuable than a system limited to highway assistance. Nvidia sees the partnership as an opportunity not only to advance the technology but also to help Volvo develop its business model around ongoing software-based offerings, he said.

items.title: Google is making inline links more prominent in AI responses
items.summary: Google is updating its AI search results to make inline links appear "higher up in responses more frequently," according to a blog post. The company's search results from AI Overviews and AI Mode give you answers in a customized view instead of the traditional list of links, but
items.content:
Links will appear ‘higher up in responses more frequently’ in Google’s AI Mode and AI Overviews.

Google is updating its AI search results to make inline links appear “higher up in responses more frequently,” according to a blog post . The company’s search results from AI Overviews and AI Mode give you answers in a customized view instead of the traditional list of links, but there are concerns that the format reduces traffic to publishers . Google says it’s been making “continued and substantial increases to the presence of inline links in our AI experiences,” and this new change will help ensure “ensure key sources are easily clickable right when you need them.”

The company is announcing several other changes to highlight links and publishers within its AI results. For sites that are among a few for a specific task or certain information — an example image from Google highlights a query about an airline refund — Google is testing showing the relevant links at the top of a response with context. For “timely” articles, the company is now rolling out the link carousels announced in May to more locations and languages. Google is making links at the end of a query “more engaging and prominent, with image thumbnails and a more clickable design.” And it’s now testing clickable links in AI mode to search profiles for publishers and creators.

Google also says that more than 400 publishers are participating in its “News AI” pilot program, which it announced in December . The licensing program pays publishers for “the delivery and use of enhanced content to develop new AI features,” including “in-depth article overviews on Google News publisher pages,” and Axios , CNN , and the Financial Times are among the partners that are newly onboard, according to Google.

items.content:
글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/10/16 02:10

빈 2026년 10월 15일 /PRNewswire/ -- 존 차이(John Cai) 화웨이(Huawei) 데이터통신 제품라인 부사장이 10월 13일 UBBF 2026 기간에 열린 Net5.5G 지능형 IP 네트워크 서밋(Net5.5G Intelligent IP Network Summit)에서 기조 연설자로 나서 불확실한 미래 속에서 AI가 확실한 기회라고 강조했다. NG WAN Solution의 대대적 구축은 NG WAN의 전면적인 상용화를 의미하는 것이며 화웨이는 업계 이해관계자들과 협력해 안전하고 복원력 있는 기반을 지속적으로 강화하고 AI 시대의 동반 성장을 이끌고자 한다고 밝혔다.

John Cai, Vice President of Huawei's Data Communication Product Line, delivering a keynote speech

화웨이의 NG WAN Solution은 장비와 링크, 서비스 계층을 아우르는 다층 보안 체계를 구축한다. 장비 계층에서는 독립적인 위협 방어 유닛(Threat Protection Unit, TPU)과 멀티모달 행동 전문가 알고리즘을 기반으로 하는 화웨이의 혁신적 RDR 솔루션이 라우터 운영체제(OS)와 분리돼 실행된다. 이를 통해 위협의 95% 이상이 탐지되고 지능형 지속 위협(APT)이 수분 내 추적된다. 데이터 평면에서는 화웨이의 독자적인 네트워크 프로세서(NP)와 지능형 플로 식별 알고리즘이 트래픽을 1:1로 검사해 수초 내 공격을 탐지하고 분산서비스거부(DDoS) 위험을 90% 줄인다. TPU는 중국의 한 메이저 통신사업자에서 3개월 넘게 사용되는 동안 8개국에서 발생한 공격 324건을 차단했다.

링크 계층에서는 모든 시나리오의 모든 화웨이 장비가 양자내성암호(PQC) 알고리즘을 지원해 암호화 성능을 40% 높여 준다. 업계 최초의 내장형 양자키분배(QKD) 솔루션은 3개 채널의 통합을 지원해 네트워크 구축 비용을 60% 절감하고 80km의 전송 거리 한계를 넘어선다. 최근 화웨이와 마카오의 한 통신사업자는 세계 최초의 양자 보안 목표 네트워크를 공개했는데 이 네트워크 덕분에 전용회선 매출이 50% 급증했다.

서비스 계층에서는 '1+4' 심층 방어를 통해 네트워크 경계의 DDoS 공격 대응 시간을 1분에서 5초 미만으로 단축해 준다. 알려지지 않은 위협의 탐지 성능을 15% 높여 주고 랜섬웨어 탐지율 100%를 달성하며, CT-SOC를 통해 위협 처리 시간을 30분 미만으로 줄여 준다.

무손실 컴퓨팅 효율: 토큰 생산성 극대화

AI가 핵심 업무에 점차 깊숙이 도입되면서 지능형 컴퓨팅은 패킷 손실에 극도로 민감해지고 있다. 단 0.1%의 손실만으로도 컴퓨팅 효율이 최대 55% 떨어질 수 있다. 화웨이의 NG WAN Solution은 AI Fabric을 활용해 네트워크 개선으로 컴퓨팅 역량을 강화해 준다. 간소화된 2계층 멀티플레인 아키텍처는 하드웨어 사용량을 30% 줄이면서 네트워크 규모를 네 배로 넓혀 준다. 네트워크 전반에 적용되는 NPLB는 링크 활용률 98%를 달성하고 학습•추론 성능을 7% 넘게 높여 준다. Starnet 무손실 알고리즘은 컴퓨팅•네트워크 시너지를 위해 1000km 초과 전송 시 패킷 손실 제로를 달성하며 원격 컴퓨팅 효율을 96% 이상으로 유지해 준다. 통신사업자는 이를 통해 로컬 환경과 유사한 경험을 제공해 기업 대상 사업의 수익화를 앞당길 수 있다. 중국의 한 통신사업자는 이 솔루션으로 의료 프로젝트를 지원해 병원의 컴퓨팅 비용을 30% 줄이는 동시에 전용회선 가입자당평균매출(ARPU)을 5배로 늘렸다.

네트워크 자율성: 네 시나리오에서 AN L4 구현

화웨이의 '1 맵, 1 브레인(One Map, One Brain)' 자율 네트워크 아키텍처는 장애 처리, 네트워크 변경, 네트워크 최적화, 보안 보호를 망라해 자율 네트워크 레벨 4(AN L4)를 구현해 준다. 네트워크 변경에서는 구성 검증과 시뮬레이션, 비교를 아우르는 폐루프 자동화를 실현한다. 보안 보호에서는 침입 탐지와 공격 추적, 원클릭 차단을 몇 분 만에 수행한다. 화웨이는 여러 통신사업자의 AN L4 달성을 지원했으며, 남아프리카공화국의 한 통신사업자는 세계 최초로 IP 네트워크에서 이 수준의 자율성을 달성하기도 했다.

전 세계에서 통신사업자 60여 곳이 NG WAN Solution을 구축했다. 이 솔루션은 무손실 컴퓨팅 효율과 다층 보안, 네트워크 자율성 분야의 지속적인 혁신을 통해 통신사업자의 AI 전략을 효율 최적화에서 가치 창출로 전환하고 AI 시대를 위한 안전하고 복원력 있는 네트워크 기반을 공고히 해 주고 있다.

화웨이는 앞으로도 업계 파트너들과 협력해 NG WAN Solution의 글로벌 도입 속도를 높이는 한편 안전하고 복원력 있으며 지능적이고 효율적인 차세대 전송망 구축을 지원해 AI 시대 통신사업자의 성장을 이끌 계획이다.

items.title: Neutron's first launch slips again amid trouble with carbon composites
items.summary: Rocket Lab announced the Neutron rocket in 2021, aiming for a first flight in 2024.
items.content:
Rocket Lab announced Wednesday that its Neutron launch vehicle won’t fly until 2027, citing an issue discovered during manufacturing of the rocket’s carbon composite structures.

The announcement was public confirmation of what nearly everyone inside Rocket Lab and the wider space industry already knew. The most recent official update from Rocket Lab in August suggested the company still held hope of delivering the first Neutron rocket to its launch pad at Wallops Island, Virginia, before the end of this year, a schedule that would have almost certainly pushed the first flight into 2027.

But Rocket Lab’s statement Wednesday about Neutron’s schedule suggests the company is still struggling with manufacturing the rocket’s large booster stage. Neutron’s reusable first stage is made of carbon composite structures, which offer low weight, high strength, and corrosion resistance. But carbon composites in aerospace are generally harder to manufacture than metallic structures.

Peter Beck, Rocket Lab’s founder and CEO, identified a manufacturing defect as the reason for Neutron’s latest schedule slip. The problem lies in the dome sections at the ends of the rocket’s first stage propellant tanks.

“Recently, we identified an issue with the manufacturing process for the propellant domes specifically, and this caused us to delay production and investigate further,” Beck said in a video released by Rocket Lab .

Engineers discovered voids, or air pockets, between layers of carbon fiber that make up the domes’ composite structure. Carbon composite manufacturing involves laying down carbon fiber layers in a mold, then curing, or heating, the material to bind the fibers together. But this is a tricky process, especially for large structures that won’t fit into an autoclave, a high-pressure thermal curing chamber common in modern aerospace factories.

The Neutron rocket’s first stage is the “largest pressurized structure ever made out of carbon composite,” Beck said. “Because of its scale, we’ve had to develop new out-of-autoclave processes to build Neutron, and this includes custom cure cycles for the very large pieces, like the forward and aft domes for the propellant tanks on Stage One.”

Inspections revealed voids in a newly cured forward dome, defects that could affect the structure’s strength, durability, and reliability, Beck said. “They don’t necessarily mean that the dome would fail in flight, but our practice is to proceed only when we believe the system has the appropriate margins.”

Engineers traced the voids to a recent design change intended to strengthen the rocket’s structure. Rocket Lab introduced the design change after a Neutron propellant tank unexpectedly ruptured during a hydrostatic pressure test in January, a failure blamed on a manufacturing defect at a “critical join” in the tank.

Officials said the failed carbon composite tank was manufactured by a “third-party contractor using a manual hand-lay process,” a decision made to allow tank testing to move forward while Rocket Lab brought online an automated fiber placement machine, which is now operational. Rocket Lab also deleted joints in the first stage tank structure and increased the thickness of some sections of the carbon composite.

“Those thicker sections are where the voids formed,” Beck said.

Rocket Lab said the problem appears to be solved after modifying the manufacturing process again. An aft propellant dome made with the updated procedure passed inspection.

“We’ve solved the problem,” Beck said. “That gives us complete confidence to move forward with the new forward dome. That process to make a new forward dome, combining with all the time that it took to investigate, identify, and resolve the issue, has pushed Neutron’s first launch date to next year.”

The Neutron rocket is significantly larger than Rocket Lab’s Electron launch vehicle, also made of carbon fiber. The light-class Electron rocket is 3.9 feet (1.2 meters) in diameter, while the medium-lift Neutron measures 23 feet (7 meters) across at its widest.

Rocket Lab completed qualification testing on Neutron’s expendable second stage and payload fairing last year. The rocket’s design is unique: The upper stage and payload rest inside the first stage’s nose cone during the initial phases of launch. A few minutes after liftoff, Neutron’s booster stage will open its clamshell-like nose cone to release the upper stage and payload to continue accelerating into orbit. Then the first stage will close its payload fairing and return to landing on an offshore platform for reuse.

Neutron’s first stage methane and liquid oxygen tanks are the largest elements of the rocket, and they must withstand internal pressure and the rigors of launch and reentry.

Rocket Lab’s checklist for the first Neutron flight is long. Final qualification of the first stage is still pending, as is qualification of the rocket’s methane-fueled Archimedes engine, nine of which will power the Neutron booster. Rocket Lab reported in August that it was heading into the “final stretch” of engine qualification testing.

Once that is complete, teams will begin the launch campaign on Virginia’s Eastern Shore. Launch campaigns for new rockets often take months before a first flight, involving multiple integrated fueling tests, countdown rehearsals, and a static fire.

Engineers often discover new problems during integrated testing, requiring repeat tests and tweaks to procedures and hardware on the launch pad and the rocket. That is the purpose of such testing.

Rocket Lab announced the Neutron rocket in 2021, aiming for a first flight in 2024. The Neutron development timeline has now doubled.

Beck said Wednesday that Neutron’s development remains “on an ambitious timeline.” In previous statements, Beck has emphasized Rocket Lab’s focus on quality and its unwillingness to launch an “unproven product.”

items.title: SK Hynix bargains for chip equipment exports to its China facility in return for building a factory in US
items.summary: SK Hynix’s Solidigm is reportedly seeking U.S. approval to send more chipmaking equipment to China as it weighs building a new NAND chip factory in America.
items.content:
SK Hynix appears to be navigating choppy U.S.-China chipmaking waters. The company’s flash memory unit, Solidigm, is seeking U.S. approval to send American chipmaking equipment to its factory in Dalian, China, as a condition to continue building a semiconductor factory in the U.S., Reuters reported , citing anonymous sources.

Solidigm has been reportedly chalking up plans to build a NAND flash memory chip factory in the U.S. and is considering upstate New York as a potential location for the facility.

NAND flash chips are primarily used in solid-state storage drives, which are employed in everything from laptops and smartphones to AI data centers. But the global component shortage, thanks to skyrocketing demand for AI data centers, has driven up prices for everything that goes into data centers, including high-speed RAM chips and SSDs. Research firm TrendForce expects NAND prices to rise 15% to 20% in the fourth quarter.

Reuters cited its sources as saying that Solidigm wants to install more chipmaking equipment in spare space at SK Hynix’s Dalian factory in China to boost NAND chip production.

SK Hynix told TechCrunch it is not seeking to expand capacity at its Dalian Mod B facility, which was completed in 2023. The chip giant added that the equipment installation is being carried out in consultation with and under authorization from the U.S. government.

Washington first imposed sweeping restrictions on advanced chips and chipmaking equipment exports to China in October 2022, citing national security concerns, and further tightened the rules in 2023 . Then in September 2025, the Trump administration revoked special export exemptions for certain SK Hynix, Samsung, and Intel facilities in China. The U.S. has since granted an annual license to Samsung and SK Hynix for sending chipmaking equipment to their plants in China.

The U.S. has also been pushing foreign chipmakers to build and expand their manufacturing facilities in America. In July, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said he wanted Samsung and SK Hynix to build chip plants in the country and that he was in talks with both companies.

Solidigm is said to be preparing for a 2027 U.S. IPO that could raise around $10 billion and value it at up to $100 billion.

items.title: Friends don’t let friends feed their data to AI agents
items.summary: There's a growing trend in the consumer tech world: gadgets designed to spy on everything and everyone around you, regardless of whether or not anyone else actually consented to it. Now, with the advent of "AI personal assistants" like Meta's Muse, you're being cheerfully asked n
items.content:
You may have consented to sharing with Muse, but all your friends sure didn’t.

There’s a growing trend in the consumer tech world: gadgets designed to spy on everything and everyone around you , regardless of whether or not anyone else actually consented to it. Now, with the advent of “AI personal assistants” like Meta’s Muse, you’re being cheerfully asked not just to give up your own data, but also the information of your friends, family, the person you went on a Hinge date with five years ago — and virtually anyone else you’ve ever come in contact with.

Since Muse was released last month, the agent has already been downloaded millions of times and hit No. 1 on Apple’s App Store. With the help of its creepy virtual avatar — a Temu Labubu-esque creature with a disarming grin — the app requests and encourages users to grant access to bank accounts, passwords, contacts, chat logs, and anything and everything that might help it to do the user’s bidding.

“These systems are advertised as autonomous helpers, genies, or servants who do what you need before you ask, seamlessly,” Meredith Whittaker, the president of the Signal Foundation, makers of the popular encrypted messaging app, told The Verge . These autonomous actions are applied “not just to the person who installed Muse on their device, but also to everyone that person communicates with, as extrapolated from their most intimate information — emails, messages, contacts, photos, and more.”

With AI agents, tech companies are letting consumers automate their everyday tasks by extending their omnivorous style of mass surveillance to massive amounts of sensitive data. It’s the same Faustian tradeoff Silicon Valley has been offering us for decades: your private data in exchange for a little bit of convenience. And for many people, the idea of having a virtual assistant that does menial tasks like filling out invoices and sending emails is compelling — especially if they don’t realize how much data they’re actually giving away in return.

“For any agent to be useful and actually help you achieve your goals, it needs to have context about you and those you interact with,” Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts told The Verge regarding other people’s data shared with Muse. “Muse gathers that based on public information and from what you’ve chosen to share, which is how it remembers the person who just sent you an invoice is in fact the plumber who you previously hired to complete some work in your bathroom or which flowers your spouse said they liked best.” Roberts pointed to Muse’s opt-in process and various options and settings that will “help people make the privacy choices that are right for them.”

“The way that the user interface is set up is designed to encourage you to share as much as possible, often more than you realize, until it’s too late.”

But not everyone has been able to navigate these options and settings. Already, users are describing incidents that are both alarming and entirely predictable. Some have reported the virtual assistant making all sorts of trouble, like grabbing millions of text messages they believed were off limits. Meta has disputed that the assistant has the ability to access text messages without permission, again attributing the incident to misconfigured app permissions and describing Muse’s ability to read text messages as “entirely opt-in.” On Threads, Meta executive David Singleton responded to a user directly , claiming that on a Mac, Muse can only gain access to the messages if the user grants the app full disk access.

In another incident, Muse gave out a tech reviewer’s home address and summoning a stranger to his apartment . In this case, the reviewer in question had given Muse permission to access that data, but simply didn’t realize it .

Eva Galperin, the director of cybersecurity for the Electronic Frontier Foundation, says these incidents are no surprise, given that AI agents like Muse are designed to confuse people into giving up as much data as possible.

“The most important takeaway is that people don’t understand what kind of data they’re handing over,” Galperin told The Verge . “The way that the user interface is set up is designed to encourage you to share as much as possible, often more than you realize, until it’s too late. It’s using dark patterns , and as a result you end up with Muse doing things that people don’t want.”

Because of the huge breadth of data AI agents like Muse are ingesting, this also means that users risk leaking not only their own sensitive information, but the information of everyone else they’ve had digital contact with.

And just like with Meta’s infamous “pervert glasses”, there’s no meaningful way to opt out — even if you’re constantly monitoring for signs that your data is compromised or your privacy is being violated. Your friends can now simply feed all of your private conservations to their virtual chatbot servants, and you’d have no way of knowing it happened.

After security researchers extracted Muse’s operating instructions, they discovered an internal process that compiles and updates profiles of every single person in a user’s life on an hourly basis. The goal of collecting all this data is to build an intimate and detailed portrait of a person’s life that forms the basis of the app’s personalized recommendations. The app tracks and measures each of the user’s private relationships, including “how close they are, what it is built on, how they act with each other, and what it seems to need right now,” and uses that data to make personalized suggestions, Wired reported.

“Meta says Muse only remembers what you choose to share. But the idea that people are making an informed choice in this case is laughable,” said Whittaker. “There is no way to assume with a straight face that the majority of people installing this system understand the consequences of using it, or the creepy dossiers that are being compiled about those they know and communicate with.”

items.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.summary: Accelerating the search for novel antimicrobial peptides using Google Antigravity for Science.
items.content:
Pengfei Tian, Maxwell L. Bileschi, Zoi Tsangalidou, Sukhdeep Singh and Lucy J. Colwell

New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process. With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier.

Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session. It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences.

This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections. The lead identified here is now undergoing wet-lab validation.

Rising antimicrobial resistance is one of the most pressing global health crises of our time and could result in an estimated 10 million annual deaths globally by 2050. To prevent this, we urgently need to discover novel therapeutics. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), particularly bacteriocins, offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics because they have naturally evolved to target fundamental vulnerabilities in competing bacteria, from cell envelopes to essential intracellular machinery, making it difficult for pathogens to develop resistance.

The exponential growth of genomic and metagenomic sequencing has populated global databases with billions of natural amino acid sequences. This pool of natural data has already produced globally used bacteriocins like Nisin, alongside recent genome-mined breakthroughs such as Darobactin, Dynobactin, and Lariocidin.

Many, however, remain locked within the unannotated "dark matter" of protein databases, with their function uncharacterized because they aren’t similar to known proteins. For example, the world's leading public resource of protein sequence and functional information, UniProt , holds millions of sequences with unknown functionality, transferred directly from genome sequencing projects.

To bridge this gap, Google developed ProtNLM (Protein Natural Language Model) , a deep learning model trained to directly read the underlying evolutionary “grammar” of amino acid sequences. This allows the model to predict biological function directly from raw protein sequences, enriching millions of previously unnamed UniProt entries with high-confidence functional labels.

Overview of the ProtNLM pipeline translating raw amino acid sequences into natural-language biological annotations for unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries. The functional annotation scope of the system covers protein names, function comments, subcellular locations, and GO terms, in addition to keywords.

Scientific discovery is rarely a single step process; finding viable candidate proteins requires human intuition and iteration to incorporate new empirical evidence. Working in Antigravity, the researcher and AI agent begin by setting a focused biological goal: find and computationally validate novel AMPs in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae . During an interactive, multi-turn session the researcher steers the scientific strategy, deciding which questions to ask and what evidence to collect, while the agent handles the heavy lifting of cross-database orchestration, structural analysis, and literature synthesis.

Navigating a vast search space:

The agent queries the database and filters millions of entries down to a handful of candidates worthy of attention. Here, the agent finds a bacteriocin (Uniprot ID: A0A0U0D591 ) with a length of 97 amino acids from the Lactococcin 972 family.

Validating the novelty of a finding:

To verify the novelty of this discovery, the researcher guides the agent to interrogate the candidate against curated knowledge in Swiss-Prot via the EMBL-EBI NCBI-BLAST service and confirm this peptide has no meaningful sequence homolog among manually reviewed proteins.

Reasoning over 3D protein structure:

The researcher steers the analysis towards structural evidence. The agent retrieves the candidate’s 3D model from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, querying it against experimentally determined structures to identify remote homologs, and superimposing the models to assess similarity. Here, the structural evidence corroborates ProtNLM’s prediction by showing the candidate's fold closely matches an experimentally determined bacteriocin. The structure viewer in Antigravity allows this structural analysis to be seamlessly performed in one place.

Reading the biological context around a gene:

The agent looks beyond the molecule itself to its genomic neighborhood, reasoning over whether the surrounding machinery supports the AMP hypothesis. Inspecting the flanking genes, it spots a revealing pattern: our previously uncharacterized candidate sits at the upstream of a tightly coupled operon, just 6 base pairs ahead of a ABC transporter permease and its potential partner ATP-binding protein, alongside another annotated bacteriocin and an XRE transcriptional regulator. This provides strong contextual evidence that it is part of a working bacteriocin system.

Building a mechanistic hypothesis from the literature :

By reviewing the existing literature, the agent proposes how the molecule might act and what pathogens it might act on. In this case, existing evidence suggests a mechanism of action targeting bacterial cell division, and a predicted potency spectrum spanning several drug-resistant pathogens.
